Definition
[sectional curvature]

↗ def:dc-ch4-2-1

1. ch4:3.2Given a point $p\in M$ and a two-dimensional subspace $\sigma \subset T_pM$, the real number $K(x,y)=K(\sigma )$, where $\{ x,y\} $ is any basis of $\sigma $, is called the sectional curvature of $\sigma $ at $p$. The importance of the sectional curvature comes from the fact that knowledge of $K(\sigma )$ for all $\sigma $ determines the curvature $R$ completely. This is a purely algebraic fact:
